claims.claim_ar: واو العطف في «وَقَالَ» تعمل كأداة ربط/استئناف تربط الكلام بما قبله أو تستأنف السرد.
claims.claim_en: The conjunction waw in «وَقَالَ» functions as an emotive/connective particle (waaw 'atifa / resumptive), linking or resuming the discourse.

claims.source_quote_ar: وجملة النداء في محل نصب مقول القول
claims.claim_ar: نداء مباشر بـ«يا» (يا فرعون) يحقق تحوّلًا في الأسلوب: من السرد إلى مخاطبة مباشرة (التفات/التخاطب).
claims.claim_en: Direct vocative with «ya» (ya Fir'awn) effects a shift in style from narration to direct address (iltifat / change of address).
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted explanatory fragment treats the structure of an addressed utterance in a different reported speech example (قالَ: يا مُوسَى...), applied here analogically to وَقَالَ مُوسَى يَا فِرْعَوْنُ.

claims.source_quote_ar: كلام مستأنف مسوق لتسلية موسى عليه السلام
claims.claim_ar: افتتاح الكلام بصيغة مستأنفة/مباشرة (كلام مستأنف مسوق) كأسلوب بلاغي لعرض القول وإبرازه.
claims.claim_en: Opening the utterance as resumed/direct speech (kalam mustanif masuq) is a rhetorical mode used to present and foreground the speech.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source chunk discusses a similar pattern in a different verse (قال: يا موسى ...); applying the characterization to this ayah is plausible but based on analogy rather than a direct commentary on S7:A104 in the provided chunks.

warnings: Provided source_chunks are grammatical/i'rab commentaries (Darwish - I'rab). They include useful remarks (e.g. 'الواو عاطفة', 'جملة النداء...') but are not the classical balagha authors listed (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir balagha). Claims are therefore drawn from i'rab-style commentary and sometimes applied analogically.

Some claims (especially the asloob_hakim / iltifat readings) are inferred by analogy from examples in the chunks (e.g. references to the pattern 'قال: يا مُوسَى...'). Verify against dedicated balagha/tafsir sources for authoritative attribution and finer nuance.
